verdict.rationale: Visa publishes per-endpoint REST reference pages for Intelligent Commerce, covering enrolling cards, initiating purchase intents and retrieving credentials. These pages list required fields, test and production hosts, and a sample mandate payload. A self-serve sandbox lets developers send test transactions, and the Trusted Agent Protocol ships a runnable reference implementation and signature code snippets. However, nothing in the evidence shows an interactive, in-browser API explorer or 'try it' console, so runnable experimentation means signing up for the sandbox or cloning repos. Missing for 10: an interactive API reference/console, runnable examples embedded in the Intelligent Commerce endpoint docs, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the docs experience.
